title: Introduction to Git Merge
overview: Git merge combines changes from one branch into another branch.

title: Performing a Merge
overview: The merge command combines another branch's changes with the current branch.

example.title: Merge Command
example.content:
git checkout main

git merge feature-login

title: Fast Forward Merge
overview: A fast-forward merge happens when the target branch has no new commits and Git can simply move the branch pointer forward.

example.title: Fast Forward
example.content:
Main
 |
 A
 |
 B
 |
 C

Pointer moves forward

title: Merge Conflicts
overview: A merge conflict occurs when Git cannot automatically combine changes made in the same part of a file.

example.title: Conflict Situation
example.content:
Branch A
   |
Same File Changed
   |
Branch B

= Merge Conflict

title: Resolving Merge Conflicts
overview: Conflicts are resolved by manually choosing the correct changes and committing the final version.

example.title: Conflict Resolution Flow
example.content:
Find Conflict
 ↓
Edit File
 ↓
Add Changes
 ↓
Commit

title: Abort Merge
overview: Git allows developers to cancel a merge operation if conflicts cannot be resolved.

title: Topic Summary
overview: You learned how merging works, different merge types, conflicts, and ways to resolve or cancel merges.

example.title: Quick Revision
example.content:
✔ Merge combines branches.
✔ Conflicts require manual fixes.
✔ Resolved conflicts need a commit.
